name: _sparse_log_softmax_backward_data
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_sparse_log_softmax_backward_data(Tensor grad_output, Tensor output, int dim, Tensor self) -> Tensor. This overload is representative only, not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract of overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and its coverage must never be narrowed to this one signature. Registered schemas (verbatim): aten::_sparse_log_softmax_backward_data(Tensor grad_output, Tensor output, int dim, Tensor self) -> Tensor ; aten::_sparse_log_softmax_backward_data.out(Tensor grad_output, Tensor output, int dim, Tensor self, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics: backward of sparse log-softmax over COO sparse tensors; given grad_output, the forward log-softmax output and the operand named self as COO tensors plus a reduction dim, it returns a COO gradient, accumulating within each normalization group identified by every sparse coordinate except the one along dim. Tested support relationships include identical, partial-overlap (documented in the pytest as covering the union of the supports), disjoint and empty supports. Overload-dependent behavior: the out variant takes out as a keyword-only COO buffer, rewrites that buffer's support and values (it does not extend it), returns the same buffer object, and reads the three inputs unchanged; the pytest asserts the returned-buffer identity and the unchanged inputs for the Gems operator. The representative default overload's registered schema declares no mutated arguments and no aliasing on its return, and Tensor(a!) annotations are representative schema metadata rather than unconditional runtime guarantees; the pytest snapshots and compares inputs only in the out-variant case. Tests additionally exercise uncoalesced duplicate coordinates, differing/partial/disjoint supports, empty operands, 0-dim and hybrid COO layouts and nan/inf values as reference comparisons, and cover rejected dtypes, out-of-range dims, dense inputs and mixed dtypes only through pytest.raises; none of that is expressed by this single-signature model.
